title: One-time Approval Token
intent: Consume narrowly bound human approval exactly once before mutation.
problem: Without HMAC-bound claims consumed under a lock, the system can accept an outcome that is not justified by the one-time approval token contract.
context: This pattern addresses one human decision authorizes one sensitive command; its concrete control is HMAC-bound claims consumed under a lock.
forces: Correctness requires that task and result fingerprints match exactly
Operational pressure can cause: expired approval authorizes a late mutation
solution: Implement HMAC-bound claims consumed under a lock. Verify the anchored symbol `ApprovalTokenDenied` with `test_token_is_bound_and_consumed_once` before reuse.
invariants: task and result fingerprints match exactly
a token identifier is consumed at most once
failure_modes: expired approval authorizes a late mutation
concurrent retries consume the token twice
security: The security boundary specifically rejects `expired approval authorizes a late mutation` and fails closed if the one-time approval token evidence cannot be verified.
privacy: For one-time approval token, persist only its decision identifiers and digests; exclude payload data unrelated to HMAC-bound claims consumed under a lock.
reuse_constraints: Confirm the target still requires: one human decision authorizes one sensitive command
Do not apply when: standing role permission is the intended policy
External Ethernian promotion signature remains mandatory
applies_when: one human decision authorizes one sensitive command
not_when: standing role permission is the intended policy
